answer: A head runs only on a quartz die the forge signs once, fused to that head for life; a die caught attesting a second head is bricked and its locked copper goes to the finder. The forge anneals one fresh die per epoch — one chamber, one firing — so an operator raising k clones waits k serial firings, one per head, a queue no capital compresses and no bulk order skips; its k-th identity costs k epochs of forge time plus plain base copper. A lone newcomer books the next firing at once.
